# PEN-3259 — the login veto read the whole pod transcript, not the result event

**Vendored files changed:** `src/server/parse.ts`, `src/server/parse.test.ts`

**Issue:** [PEN-3259](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-3259) · **PR:** [#1868](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1868)

Stopped `isClaudeTransientUpstreamError`'s LOGIN VETO reading the whole pod transcript. The mirror image of PEN-3223 (the last row in the now-frozen `PROVENANCE-CHANGES.md`): that change narrowed the *granting* haystack, and explicitly left the veto wide on the argument that a veto can only ever SUPPRESS the transient label, so narrowing it would *widen* what the function grants. That argument is sound about direction and silent about cost, and the cost is what this measures. `detectClaudeLoginRequired` joins `parsed.result` + `parsed.errors[]` + `stdout` + `stderr`, and `stdout` is the entire pod log — so a run that merely *mentions* auth vetoes its own true capacity refusal. Measured over 446 failed runs carrying a terminal result event (retained logs from 2026-09-12; 403 x281, 429 x95, 503 x70): the transcript-reading veto fires **91** times, the bounded-surface veto **0**. Not one run in the corpus reports an auth failure on its own result event, so every firing was transcript-only, and 89 of the 91 are the bare word `unauthorized` — which an agent reading a 401 handler, or this very issue's text, writes into its own transcript. What the narrowing admits is enumerated rather than counted: 27 runs move from no retry family at all to `transient_upstream` — 19 Penstock capacity refusals, each carrying an explicit reset timestamp, and 8 Anthropic 503s. **No 403 is admitted and no run loses a transient label.** `detectClaudeLoginRequired` itself is UNCHANGED, deliberately: it is shared, and `stdout` is the right surface for its other callers, which ask whether a run needs re-authentication before any result event exists. What changed is what this one rule passes it, gated on the terminal result event so the no-result-event path keeps the transcript read — that is where a login prompt actually appears. The `claude-local` twin gets the same change and is the MORE exposed copy: over the same 446 transcripts its regex fires 308 times against this copy's 91, with `failed to authenticate` — ordinary git/gh/ssh/registry output — accounting for 285 on its own. 

**Stacking order is load-bearing, not cosmetic.** On the pre-PEN-3223 wide haystack this narrowing *alone* takes the transient label from 237 runs to 301 and the 403s inside it from 99 to 136, i.e. it makes that defect worse; with PEN-3223 in front of it the 403s go to 0. Do not cherry-pick this ahead of PEN-3223. Recorded as a per-change entry rather than an integrity-hash recompute: this branch was restacked onto PEN-3223's linearized head after BLO-35109 withdrew the stored hash, so the hash regeneration its commit message originally described no longer exists to perform.
